extracted.intended_audience: corporate communications and public relations professionals responsible for crisis messaging and press releases
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for drafting and sequencing press releases and public statements during a corporate or institutional crisis, specifying timing, content, spokesperson roles, verification, and update cadence to preserve or rebuild trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgment within 2 hours
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledgment (Hours 0-2) — Brief statement acknowledging the issue; 'We are aware and investigating'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make a very short, timely acknowledgment within the first two hours. Use plain language such as 'We are aware and investigating.' Do not speculate; set expectations for updates and designate a single spokesperson.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brief statement acknowledging the issue
rubrics_metrics.description: A concise initial message that confirms awareness of the incident without speculation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the first release terse and factual. Avoid conjecture or detailed explanations until facts are verified. Example phrasing provided: 'We are aware and investigating.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Designated single spokesperson
rubrics_metrics.description: Single spokesperson designated to speak on behalf of the organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Name one authoritative spokesperson early to provide a consistent voice. Ensure spokesperson has access to verified information and authority to speak about next steps; make them reachable to media and stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Update cadence specified and honored
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify how often updates will be provided and then follow that schedule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tell stakeholders when you will provide the next update (e.g., hourly, daily) and ensure communications teams honor the promised cadence — failing to update erodes trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid speculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not speculate about causes, motives, or impacts in early communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If information is incomplete, state what is known and what is under investigation. Avoid guessing or offering unverified explanations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific facts as known
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide specific facts rather than vague, general statements as information is confirmed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer concrete details (who, what, when, where) that have been verified. Stakeholders demand specific actions and facts, not values-based or generic language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeline of events (initial)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a timeline of events as they are known in the initial response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include key timestamps and sequence of occurrences in initial reporting so stakeholders understand what happened and when.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate corrective actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe immediate steps the organization is taking to stop harm or contain the issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List concrete, short-term actions implemented right away (e.g., systems taken offline, services suspended, recalls initiated). Avoid vague promises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakeholder communication plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Have and communicate a plan for how impacted stakeholders will be informed and supported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify affected groups and channels (customers, employees, regulators) and outline how and when each will be reached. Ensure plans address their specific concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dedicated media contact
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a clear media contact for press inquiries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include name, role, phone and email for a dedicated media contact in releases so journalists and stakeholders can obtain verified information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive timeline (substantive response)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the substantive response (Days 1-7) present a full and comprehensive timeline of events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expand the initial timeline into a detailed chronology that reflects investigations and findings; update as new verified facts emerge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary root cause analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an initial/root cause analysis when available (labeled preliminary if not final).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Share what the organization currently believes to be the root cause, clearly distinguishing preliminary findings from final determinations; commit to further investigation if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed corrective actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Outline detailed corrective actions the organization will take to remedy the issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include short-term fixes and the steps toward remediation; be specific about what will change and who is responsible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent oversight or verification when relevant
rubrics_metrics.description: Bring in independent oversight/verification where applicable and indicate it in communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When third-party review or audits are appropriate, announce them and share their scope; independent verification increases credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-term commitments (measurable)
rubrics_metrics.description: Make long-term commitments and ensure they are measurable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commit to concrete, time-bound improvements (policy changes, investments, programs) and state how progress will be measured and reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome reporting (resolution phase)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report outcomes once the situation is resolved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Share final findings, what was done to remediate, and results of any follow-up actions or verifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lessons learned
rubrics_metrics.description: Communicate what the organization learned from the incident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outline changes to processes or systems and how the organization will prevent recurrence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy and practice changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Announce changes to policies or practices prompted by the crisis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail specific policy or operational changes and timelines for implementation to demonstrate institutional learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakeholder follow-through
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure and communicate follow-through with affected stakeholders after resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe steps taken to make affected parties whole or to mitigate harm, and provide channels for ongoing support or inquiries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Named accountability (not 'the company')
rubrics_metrics.description: Use named accountability rather than impersonal corporate phrasing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify responsible teams, leaders, or decision-makers when appropriate; avoid hiding behind faceless corporate language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concrete actions over aspirational language
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritize concrete actions instead of values statements or aspirational rhetoric.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholders expect actionable steps; statements of values without accompanying actions erode trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: CEO visibility and accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: CEO visible and accessible during the crisis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visible senior leadership (including the CEO when appropriate) signals seriousness and commitment. Ensure leaders are prepared and authentic in engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentic communication (avoid PR-speak)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authentic communication outperforms polished 'PR-speak'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use empathetic, plain-language messaging rather than lawyered or overly sanitized statements that strip empathy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent verification where possible
rubrics_metrics.description: Seek and cite independent verification to support claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third-party confirmation (audits, investigations) strengthens credibility. If verification is pending, be transparent about that status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid generic 'we take this seriously' language
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not rely on generic statements like 'we take this seriously'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such phrases are trust-eroding unless paired with specifics and actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not apologize without specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid apologies that lack concrete explanations of what went wrong and what will be done.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apologies should be accompanied by facts, accountability, and corrective steps; vague apologies can worsen perceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not deflect blame onto victims or others
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid shifting blame to victims, partners, or external parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Blame deflection undermines credibility and damages trust; own what is within your control and clearly explain outside factors if relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid lawyered language that strips empathy
rubrics_metrics.description: Lawyerly, overly cautious language that removes empathy erodes trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance legal risk management with human, empathetic communication; coordinate with legal but prioritize clear, humane messages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respond quickly (avoid slow response or silence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quick response is essential; silence or delayed responses erode trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish monitoring and rapid-response processes so the organization can acknowledge and begin communicating promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honor update commitments (avoid failing to update)
rubrics_metrics.description: Failing to update on progress after promising to do so undermines credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an update cadence is promised, adhere to it; if plans change, explain why and set a new cadence.

rubrics_metrics.name: CEO leadership expected on social issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Stakeholders expect visible CEO leadership on social issues during crises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leaders should be prepared to speak to social implications when relevant; inaction or absence can be read negatively.
